Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

attack verb and noun

in words

also criticize, lash out at, verbal attack, rail at, inveigh against

classical

Cic. Q. fr. 2.3.3: vehementer est in Pompejum invectus
Cic. Fam. 12.25.4: sīc sum in Antōnium invectus

invehor, invehī, invectus sum

the passive of invehō, with in and the accusative, conjugation

attack in words, inveigh against

Other words

  • oppugnō, oppugnāre, oppugnāvī, oppugnātum — attack, oppose (a person, a proposal)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Cic. Fam. 5.2.6: nōn oportuisse Metellum … oppugnārī ā mē (Lewis & Short); Traupman 274

  • īnsector, īnsectārī, īnsectātus sum — hound, rail at

    verb, first conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Cic. Fin. 2.80: aliquem maledictīs īnsectārī (Lewis & Short)

  • impugnō, impugnāre, impugnāvī, impugnātum — attack, assail

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Sall. J. 29.2: ā prīncipiō ācerrimē rēgem impugnāverat (Lewis & Short); Traupman 148, 274: competītōrēs suōs inpugnat, he attacks his opponents

Examples

  • eō diē Catō vehementer est in Pompejum invectus et eum ōrātiōne perpetuā tamquam reum accūsāvit

    that day Cato attacked Pompey fiercely and accused him in a long speech as though he were on trialCic. Q. fr. 2.3.3

  • sīc sum in Antōnium invectus ut ille nōn ferret

    I attacked Antony so hard that he could not bear itCic. Fam. 12.25.4

See also attack.
